<!-- pr-reviewer: 9170c895039d3fe9eb8d6970ea37a28d897627e2 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The LF rule covers the root and catalog example programs. The checkout test checks every tracked example NC file.
The decision record explains the choice. The body includes `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `PROCESS_VERSION`.

Local results after a clean trial merge with upstream main `c42eeba78b1078093bcc874f0a560d620e74ffe7`:

- `cargo test -p xtask --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p xtask --test example_line_endings`: 1 passed.
- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask`: 163 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.
- All four tracked example NC files show `i/lf w/lf` and `text eol=lf`.

Mutation check: I used separate temporary repositories with `core.autocrlf=true`.
The upstream attributes produced CRLF in the catalog, first-part, and first-router-part programs. This was the expected failure.
The PR attributes preserved LF and index bytes in all four programs. This was the expected pass.
No PR files changed during this check.

The PR changes no posted NC bytes, geometry, collision checks, gouge checks, or stock simulation. No goldens moved.
It changes no UI files. Screenshots are not required.

Requested before merge: none.

Limits: Tests ran on Linux. No Windows host test ran. App and site suites did not run.
The gate dry run selected unrelated upstream changes because the trial merge was uncommitted. I ran the relevant xtask checks directly.
No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
